definition: Small data files placed on your device by websites other than the one you're currently visiting, typically used for tracking your browsing behavior across multiple sites.
metaDescription: Learn about third party cookies - tracking files that follow you across websites to collect data about your browsing habits and online behavior.
simpleExplanation: When you visit a website, other companies (not the website owner) can also place cookies on your device. These third party cookies track you as you browse different websites, building a profile of your interests and online activities.
whyItMatters: Third party cookies enable extensive cross-site tracking, allowing companies to build detailed profiles of your browsing habits, interests, and online behavior without your explicit knowledge or consent.
technicalDetail: Third party cookies are set by domains different from the one in your browser's address bar, typically through embedded content like ads, social media buttons, or analytics scripts. They persist across websites, enabling advertisers and data brokers to track users' complete browsing journeys.

examples.explanation: You browse shoes on an online store, then visit a news website and see ads for the exact shoes you viewed, delivered through third party advertising cookies.
Facebook's Like button on various websites sets third party cookies that track your visits across different sites, even if you don't click the button or have a Facebook account.
Google Analytics cookies track your journey across multiple websites that use the service, building a comprehensive view of your browsing patterns and interests.
